subject: food-science
intro: Food science is applied chemistry, biology and engineering aimed at the plate, leading to work formulating products, keeping supply chains safe and regulating what the labels say.

roles.title: Food Scientists and Technologists
roles.what: Study the principles behind the processing and deterioration of foods, analyse food content for vitamins, fat, sugar and protein, discover new food sources, and find the best ways to process, package, preserve, store and distribute food.
roles.where: Food chemistry's water activity and macronutrients, the processing-and-preservation methods of unit 4, and the product-development unit are the core competencies the role exercises daily.

roles.title: Food Science Technicians
roles.what: Work with food scientists to run standardised qualitative and quantitative tests on food and beverage products, assisting research and development in quality control, packaging, processing and use of foods.
roles.where: HACCP and food-safety testing from unit 3, sensory-science panels from unit 6, and rheology and texture from the food-engineering unit give you the measurement and quality-control bench skills the job is made of.

roles.title: Agricultural Technicians
roles.what: Assist agricultural scientists in plant and animal research, collecting samples and running tests that improve crop yield and quality — the raw-material side of the food industry.
roles.where: Pathogens in the food supply and spoilage organisms from the food-microbiology unit, plus the traceability and recalls topic, connect raw-material testing to the safety work processors rely on.

roles.title: Agricultural Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in the agricultural sciences, including food science and technology, combining lectures and laboratories with research into food systems.
roles.where: The IFT competency arc of this course — chemistry, microbiology, safety, engineering, product development and regulation — is the curriculum food-science programmes are accredited to teach.
